text:
maya: thinking out loud — do we want a lightweight "exemption" layer for specific model families during short-lived canaries? e.g., allow a small burst above per-model caps for 10m while a new variant ramps.
chris: yep would help early validation. question is: safe default TTL and how to prevent abuse.
noah: what about tying exemptions to rollout objects so they auto-expire and are visible in console? then we can audit and revoke.
leila: agree. UX should show active exemptions next to the quota graph. make it obvious "temporary" and link to rollout ID.
maya: rough proposal: exemption = { org_id, model_family, delta_tokens_per_min, expires_at, rollout_id, requested_by }. require manager approval for > X tokens.
chris: implementation caveat: our leaky-bucket limiter currently enforces per-key + per-model-family. We can layer exemption as a short-circuit that increases the bucket capacity for matching keys. but need to think about billing and telemetry.
noah: billing: mark tokens consumed under exemption with event tag "exempt=true" and store applied_delta so we can reconcile cost. console should show both metered and exempted token counts.
leila: telemetry: add events: exemption.requested, exemption.approved, exemption.applied, exemption.revoked. include rollout_id and approver. keep events small to avoid high-cardinality blowup.
maya: security: restrict who can request exemptions in RBAC. default: writers can request up to small delta, admins can approve larger. audit log required.
chris: edge case: what if model family variant changes shape (e.g., different seq len) mid-exemption? we should pin exemption to model family + model-size-tag or explicitly to model version if rollout_id provided.
noah: alternative: rather than bump capacity, we could provide a loaning mechanism where a small shared pool (per-org) lends credits to models temporarily and the pool is replenished slowly. simpler accounting but changes user-visible quotas.
leila: loan pool sounds interesting for teams that want elastic headroom without per-rollout approvals. but we need tenant fairness rules. maybe priority tiers: "canary" loans get lower priority than "prod" loans.
maya: can we sketch config examples for both approaches?
chris: sure, exemption object example:
```json
{ "org_id": "org_123", "model_family": "redwood-xl", "delta_tpm": 5000, "expires_at": "2026-05-01T12:30:00Z", "rollout_id": "rl_987", "requested_by": "maya" }
```
noah: loan-pool config example:
```yaml
org_id: org_123
loan_pool:
  capacity_tokens: 200000
  replenish_rate_tpm: 1000
  priority_rules:
    - tag: canary
      max_share: 0.2
    - tag: prod
      max_share: 0.8
```
leila: ops question: metrics we care about: applied_exemptions_count, exempted_tokens_total, loan_pool_utilization, exemption_approval_latency. also show per-model-family breakdown.
chris: runtime enforcement: we need quick lookups. maybe maintain an in-memory exemption table keyed by (org_id, model_tag) with TTLs and a generation id so config changes are fast. fallback to persistent store if miss.
maya: console flow: Request exemption -> show pending card under "Active Rollouts" -> show status (pending/approved/auto-expired) -> link to revoke. also allow scheduled auto-revoke at rollout end.
noah: A/B test plan: enable exemptions for 10% of orgs, track error spike, latency, and cost delta. set rollback threshold on cost increase or error increase.
leila: QA: simulate high concurrent canaries across models to ensure our ordering doesn't starve prod traffic. we must enforce global priority caps.
chris: one more: API surface. /v1/exemptions POST returns exemption_id; GET /v1/exemptions?org=org_123 lists active/past. enforcement part attaches header X-Exemption: exemption_id on downstream requests for tracing.
maya: love that. add UI audit link to click-through to exemption details.
opsbot: automated note: "Exemption system design conversation logged. Remember to create follow-up ticket ENG-PLAT-9923 for RBAC + console surfaces." :credit_card: 
noah: next steps: I'll prototype the in-memory table + header propagation. chris can wire up limiter to consult table. leila will prototype console mockups. maya will draft RBAC + approval thresholds.
maya: thanks team, aiming to sync next Tuesday.
leila: yup, added to calendar.
chris: pulling branch names: feature/exemptions-lookup + feature/exemption-api. I'll open PRs early next week.
noah: I'll add telemetry events to schemas and forward to kinesis.
maya: if anyone hits urgent concerns, ping me directly. :rocket:
